title: November 20 — a world with winding, and a camera that left the lab
summary: Two newly reviewed projects grow the census from 665 to 667. ComplexClockfield tests topology, structural clocks and the difference between history-dependent nonlinear responses and vortex-specific memory. WIFIcam is a separately installable Android Camera2 server with browser and Windows desktop controls, independent of LightScan.

nodes.claim: Interactive complex Mexican-hat field Ψ=u+iv with measured +/− phase winding, static or adaptive structure-based effective inertia, and controlled AB/BA probe experiments; an identity lab separately tests vortex survival, history-sensitive response and core-transplant interventions.
nodes.survived: In deterministic tests a +1 winding remained detectable after a bounded impulse (+1→+1, ~2-cell displacement). The linear sham-subtracted AB/BA response is effectively zero, while nonlinear systems can respond differently after AB and BA. A core-region transplant can change later probe response.
nodes.killed: No demonstrated particle-specific memory or advantage for a slowed structural clock: nonlinear vacuum can show stronger history sensitivity, both vortex and vacuum transplants become donor-like, and the tested graded-clock vortex trails its uniform-clock control. Finite pinned boundaries and one deterministic configuration do not prove free particles, gravity or cognition.
nodes.era: November 20: clocks, winding and a practical camera

nodes.claim: Installable Android Camera2 camera server with a token-protected Wi-Fi URL, live browser controls and a Windows Tkinter GUI for camera/lens choice, zoom, manual focus, ISO, shutter, white balance, torch, still JPEG and bursts.
nodes.survived: The project provides native Android source, a directly downloadable debug APK, a self-contained browser interface, a desktop Python controller and screenshots. Local LAN operation is independent of LightScan and does not need a cloud account.
nodes.killed: Not a universal replacement for phone camera firmware: usable physical cameras and manual controls are device-dependent, the phone app must stay awake in the foreground, HTTP is unencrypted, and source-reported operation is not a cross-device compatibility benchmark.

edges.why: ComplexClockfield explicitly revisits Clockfield's idea that field structure changes effective local oscillator timescales; the new engine uses a two-component complex scalar and exposes uniform/stamped/adaptive controls.
The source README and theory explicitly contrast the older real-scalar PhiWorld peaks with phase-winding defects in the new complex field; conceptual continuation, not asserted code inheritance.

The earlier phone-camera setup motivated separate, reusable camera control; the resulting native Camera2 app and Windows interface stand on their own. This is a practical spinout, not a LightScan runtime dependency or port of its inverse code.

motifs.title: A surviving defect is not the same as a remembering individual
motifs.description: ComplexClockfield separates charge survival from counterfactual nonlinear readout and transplantation. Its nonlinear-vacuum controls prevent attributing generic nonlinear memory to a vortex.

motifs.title: A reusable instrument can leave its original experiment
motifs.description: WIFIcam turns phone-camera acquisition into a standalone local Android and Windows camera controller. The tool has practical value even when the LightScan optical inverse remains unresolved.
